title.suggested: Stakeholder Allen's Views on the Sharpe-Crosby Match

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reported that Tom Allen, stakeholder of the $1,000 for the Sharpe-Crosby fight, would try to get bail for the jailed Sharpe and wanted the match postponed so both men got a square deal.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Wednesday Morning, November 1, 1893, page 5.

facts.fact: Allen was stakeholder for the Sharpe-Crosby fight, holding the $1,000 posted by the backers and empowered to name the time and place if no club offered a suitable purse
Allen said he would try to secure bail bonds for the imprisoned Sharpe and offered a cash guarantee
facts.quote: I will see my brewer this morning and make a last effort to get bonds for Sharpe. I am willing to put up a cash guarantee, and if we can find an owner of real estate in Illinois who will consent to go bail for him we will have him out.

facts.fact: Allen urged postponing the fight to early December, citing his own experience
facts.quote: A man can't step out of prison into a ring and do himself justice. I have had experience and know what I am talking about.

facts.fact: Allen said he would see both fighters treated fairly with the stake money
facts.quote: I have the $1,000 the men's backers posted, and, while I do not say what I will do with it, I am determined to see that both men get a square deal.

notes: Sharpe and Crosby had fought earlier at Nameoki, Illinois; Sharpe was jailed awaiting trial at Edwardsville.
